transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I've been struggling with this constant feeling that people are watching and monitoring me. It feels like there are groups of people tracking my every move, and I just can

Have you also had times when your mood was unusually high or irritable with lots of energy, or times when you felt very depressed? If so, did those mood changes happen only when the feeling of being watched was present, or at other times too?

I've never had high or irritable energy, but I've been feeling deeply depressed, sad, and exhausted for the past three months. The feeling of being monitored actually started before that, about five months ago. This means there were several weeks at the beginning where I felt watched but my mood was still normal.
Besides feeling watched, have you had any other symptoms like hearing voices, seeing things others don’t, or feeling that your thoughts are being controlled or interfered with?

Yes, I do sometimes hear voices whispering when no one is around, and I've occasionally seen shadows or figures that others can't see. However, I don't feel like anyone is controlling or interfering with my thoughts.
Since your depression began, have there been at least 2 weeks when the voices or feeling of being watched continued even though your mood was back to normal or not depressed?

Yes, there have been times like that. There was a period of about three weeks where my mood actually felt relatively normal and I wasn't feeling depressed, but I still heard the whispering and felt like I was being watched.
Over the full time you’ve been ill, have the depression symptoms been present for most of the illness, or have the psychotic symptoms happened mostly on their own?

The depression symptoms have definitely been present for most of the overall time I've been struggling. However, there were still those periods, like the few weeks at the very beginning and that other time I mentioned, where the voices and the feeling of being watched were happening completely on their own without the depression.
Since these symptoms started, have they caused a clear drop in how you function day to day, like trouble keeping up with work, school, relationships, or taking care of yourself?

I'm not really sure, to be honest, and I haven't thought about whether my day-to-day functioning has dropped. I've just been trying to get through each day, so I haven't really paid attention to that.
Can you tell me whether, since this started, you’ve had problems at work or school, pulled away from other people, or had more trouble taking care of yourself than before?

Yes, I have definitely pulled away from my friends and family and have been withdrawing from people over the past few months. I've also had a really hard time keeping up with my work and daily tasks because I just don't have the energy or motivation, and I feel constantly exhausted.
Even during times when you were not feeling depressed, did you still have low motivation, reduced emotional expression, or social withdrawal?

Yes, even during those times when my mood was okay, I still had no motivation to do anything and felt very shut off from other people. These struggles with my motivation and withdrawing from others have actually been going on for about five months, which is longer than the depression itself.
During the depressed periods, did you also have symptoms like loss of interest, changes in sleep or appetite, feelings of guilt or worthlessness, or thoughts of death or suicide?

Yes, during those depressed times, I completely lost interest in all of my usual hobbies and activities. I didn't have any changes in my sleep or appetite, though, and I haven't felt guilty or had any thoughts of suicide.
For those depressed periods, did the sadness and loss of interest last most of the day nearly every day for at least 2 weeks?

Yes, the sadness and flat mood have been constant, lasting nearly all day, every day, for about three months now. I have completely lost interest in absolutely everything, and it just doesn't seem to lift at all. It is incredibly exhausting to live with this every single day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions, auditory hallucinations, visual perceptual disturbances) plus a major depressive episode that has been present for most of the total illness duration. There were also at least 2 weeks of psychotic symptoms in the absence of depression, which supports schizoaffective disorder rather than major depressive disorder with psychotic features. Compared with schizophrenia, the prominent depressive syndrome occupying most of the illness favors schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.
